Let me analyze the user stories:

- U1: Invoke REST APIs via shell to validate StreamController operations — this is building a shell (CLI) for spring-cloud-data that talks to the REST API (Spring Shell based). Effort: moderate.
- U2: Adapt redis counter from XD (Spring XD) to s-c-s (spring-cloud-stream) module — port a counter module (Redis counter) as a Spring Cloud Stream module (spring-cloud-stream-modules). Small-to-moderate.
- U3: Setup CI infrastructure for spring-cloud-data repo — Jenkins/Travis CI setup, build plans, etc. Small.
- U4: Resolve and add module dependent JARs to Boot loader — handle external libraries (e.g., database drivers) required by OOTB modules. This involves Maven dependency resolution (Aether) and Spring Boot launcher classloader work. Moderate-to-large, somewhat research-heavy.
- U5: Bootify ModuleLauncher — refactor ModuleLauncher to use Spring Boot for property handling, options, CP (classpath) augmentation. Moderate.
- U6: Investigate approach to port PHD (Pivotal HD) as provider for HDFS module from XD — an investigation/spike to decide HDFS dependency handling in root classpath. This is research/spike. Small-moderate (spike).
- U7: Add REST support for stream commands — REST endpoints for stream commands backed by StreamController (create, deploy, undeploy, destroy streams, list). Moderate.
- U8: Setup CI infrastructure for spring-cloud-stream-modules repo. Small.

technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline stack: Java 17, Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3.x, Maven as build tool, consistent with the Spring requirements stated in the specification.
U1 (shell): implement the CLI with Spring Shell; REST communication with the s-c-d server via a RestTemplate-based client layer encapsulating all StreamController endpoints.

U2 (redis counter): port the Spring XD redis counter module as a standalone Spring Cloud Stream module in the spring-cloud-stream-modules repo, using Spring Data Redis and the s-c-s binder abstraction; keep the XD counter semantics (named counters, increment/decrement) so dashboards can consume them.
U3/U8 (CI): use a Jenkins pipeline (Jenkinsfile committed to each repo) with commit webhooks, Maven verify builds, unit test reporting, and snapshot artifact publishing to repo.spring.io.

U4 (external libs in Boot loader): resolve module-dependent JARs (e.g., JDBC drivers) at module launch/deployment time using Maven Aether; rely on Spring Boot's PropertiesLauncher-based classpath augmentation so external libraries are added to the module classpath without repackaging OOTB module JARs.

U5 (bootify ModuleLauncher): refactor ModuleLauncher to bootstrap modules with SpringApplication; use @ConfigurationProperties with relaxed binding for module options/properties to enable future options and classpath augmentation features.

U6 (PHD/HDFS): treat as a time-boxed investigation spike only; deliverable is a decision report on loading Pivotal HD (PHD) HDFS client dependencies into the root classpath at runtime (launcher-based vs. shaded vs. container-provided), not a production implementation.

U7 (REST for stream commands): implement stream lifecycle endpoints (create, list, status, deploy, undeploy, destroy) as Spring MVC controllers delegating to StreamController, with JSON/HAL responses consistent with the existing s-c-d REST layer.
assumptions: One experienced developer performs all work, already familiar with the Spring ecosystem and with access to the Spring XD codebase for porting reference.
The spring-cloud-data repository already contains a StreamController skeleton and basic domain model; the spring-cloud-stream-modules repository exists with a build/module template.
A Jenkins server and required credentials/repos are available; CI work covers pipeline configuration and build jobs, not provisioning of the CI server hardware.
A Redis instance and a PHD/HDFS test environment are available for integration testing and the spike.
Estimates are effort in workdays (8h), including design, implementation, unit tests, and self-review, but excluding elapsed calendar time (CI run waits, review feedback cycles).
U6 is scoped as an investigation spike producing a written recommendation; no production HDFS module code is included.
The user stories are written in early spring-cloud-data/stream terms ({{...}} markup, XD porting); interpretation follows the stated intent of each story.

activities.activity_name: Overall solution design and work planning
activities.activity_description: Review all user stories, study relevant Spring XD code (counter, module launching, HDFS), define module/repo structure, API surface, and sequencing of work.

activities.activity_name: U1: Design shell command model and REST client layer
activities.activity_description: Define shell commands mapping to StreamController operations; design RestTemplate-based client abstraction, error handling and output formatting for the s-c-d shell.

activities.activity_name: U1: Implement shell commands for StreamController operations
activities.activity_description: Implement Spring Shell commands invoking the s-c-d REST API so developers can validate StreamController operations from the command line.

activities.activity_name: U1: Shell unit and integration tests
activities.activity_description: Write unit tests for command parsing/REST client and integration tests against a running s-c-d server.

activities.activity_name: U2: Port redis counter module from XD to spring-cloud-stream
activities.activity_description: Adapt the XD redis counter as an s-c-s module in spring-cloud-stream-modules using Spring Data Redis and the binder abstraction, preserving counter semantics for dashboard feeds.
Unit tests plus integration tests against a live Redis instance validating counter increments/decrements within a streaming pipe.

activities.activity_name: U3: Set up CI infrastructure for spring-cloud-data repo
activities.activity_description: Create Jenkins pipeline for spring-cloud-data: commit-triggered builds, Maven verify, test reporting, snapshot publishing, and notifications.

activities.activity_name: U4: Design module dependency resolution and Boot loader integration
activities.activity_description: Design how external libraries (e.g., database drivers) required by OOTB modules are resolved (Aether) and added to the Boot loader classpath at launch time.

activities.activity_name: U4: Implement JAR resolution and Boot loader packaging
activities.activity_description: Implement Aether-based resolution of module-dependent JARs and their inclusion via PropertiesLauncher-based classpath augmentation in the Boot loader.

activities.activity_name: U4: Validation tests with external libraries
activities.activity_description: Verify the approach with representative external libraries (e.g., JDBC drivers) for OOTB modules; unit and integration tests.
Refactor ModuleLauncher onto Spring Boot: SpringApplication bootstrap, @ConfigurationProperties-based option/property binding, groundwork for future classpath augmentation.
Tests covering property/option binding, module launch behavior, and regression checks against existing launcher behavior.

activities.activity_name: U6: Investigate PHD provider approach for HDFS module (spike)
activities.activity_description: Time-boxed spike: evaluate options for loading PHD HDFS client dependencies into the root classpath at runtime; prototype the leading option and write a decision report.

activities.activity_name: U7: Design REST API for stream commands
activities.activity_description: Define resources, endpoints, request/response formats for stream lifecycle commands (create, list, status, deploy, undeploy, destroy).

activities.activity_name: U7: Implement REST endpoints backed by StreamController
activities.activity_description: Implement Spring MVC controllers exposing stream commands, delegating to StreamController, with validation and consistent error handling.
Unit tests (MockMvc) and integration tests covering the stream command endpoints.

activities.activity_name: U8: Set up CI infrastructure for spring-cloud-stream-modules repo
activities.activity_description: Create Jenkins pipeline for the s-c-s-m repo: commit-triggered builds, Maven verify across modules, test reporting, snapshot publishing.
Update READMEs and reference docs: shell usage, redis counter module options, external library handling, bootified launcher properties, REST endpoints, CI setup.
Cross-feature validation (shell driving REST stream commands with modules launched by the bootified launcher and external libs), defect fixing, final hardening.
